subject_session: all 15 sessions, 5 mice (LA3/LA8/LA9/LA11/LA12); GLM/example figs use sub-LA11_ses-1
stated_limitation: Two limitations follow from the stimulus set. The five tones are spaced a full octave apart, so tuning bandwidth is barely resolved: a half-width could be measured for only 774 of the 1,564 units, with a median of 1.1 octaves, and for the rest the curve had not fallen to half its peak by the neighbouring tone. All tones were played at a single level (60 dB SPL), so this is one slice through the frequency response area rather than the area itself, and level-dependent effects cannot be seen.

justification.dataset: 000986 is a known-good, standard choice for auditory frequency tuning: mouse auditory cortex Neuropixels during passive pure-tone presentation.
justification.handling: Real data streamed from DANDI S3 via remfile, trial-aligned with matched reordering of onsets/freq, response window taken from the measured population latency, all 15 sessions across 5 mice.
justification.analysis: Per-unit ANOVA and Wilcoxon tests, split-half cross-validated BF (avoiding selection bias), cross-validated Poisson naive-Bayes decoding, and a NeMoS GLM with interleaved-block CV comparing frequency-specific vs frequency-blind models.
justification.correctness: Every reported quantity reproduces exactly from the committed npz files and figures, and the numbers are internally consistent and statistically sound.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, example units are genuinely representative strong tuners, and cross-validated versions are shown throughout.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate; the write-up names the octave-spacing and single-level limitations, notes the GLM pseudo-R2 is small either way, explains why split-half CV is needed, and documents a rejected dataset with a negative control.
